Figure 4-2. Problem File Organization. 
Each trajectory in a problem is identified with a unique trajectory number and name. 
The trajectory number is used within TAOS to identify each trajectory. Both the tra- 
jectory number and name appear on output files to identify each trajectory. 
Within a trajectory7 each segment is identified with a unique segment number. Al- 
though a descriptive title can be given for a segment, it is not used to identify the seg- 
ment. The segment numbers must be unique within a trajectory7 but different trajec- 
tories can use the same set of segment numbers. 
The following problem file defines a simple trajectory: 
(pullout 
1 
*title 
Example of a maneuvering trajectory 
*atmos standard 
*earth wgs-84 
*trajectory 1 rv start on 1 
*initial geodetic 
long=O . 0 
lat=O .O 
psi=90.0 
time=O . O  
alt=300000

*print time alt range mach vel gamgd dynprs alpha ca cn 
*segment 1 Ballistic flight 
*aero ca=(rv,ca) 
cn=(rv-cn)
